definitions.definition: Xn=ℝ^n with the standard orthonormal coordinates indexed by j=1,…,n, its Euclidean norm and inner product, and its standard topology.

Ym=ℝ^m with its standard Euclidean norm |y|=sqrt(Σ_k y_k²) and real inner product ⟨y,z⟩=Σ_k y_k z_k; k runs from 1 to m. All inner products and vector norms below use the corresponding standard real Euclidean structures.
Ω={(x,t)∈Xn×ℝ : t>0}. Positive-time differentiation means ordinary differentiation in this open domain, with no assertion at t=0.
ũ(x,t)=u(x,t) when t>0 and ũ(x,t)=q when t≤0. This only specifies a total representation of u; no regularity at nonpositive times is asserted.

For real normed spaces A,B, a function f:A→B, a point z∈A and a direction v∈A, write D_v f(z)=Df(z)[v]=fderiv ℝ f z v. Here Df(z) is the continuous linear Fréchet derivative when it exists, and the total fderiv convention gives the zero continuous linear map otherwise. This notation alone asserts no differentiability.

b_std is the standard orthonormal basis; its jth vector, written b_j for j=1,…,n, has jth coordinate 1 and other coordinates 0. Fin n indices 0,…,n−1 are an equivalent relabeling with the same Euclidean structures and volume.

definitions.type: family of constant spatial directions in Xn×ℝ

definitions.definition: On Ω set u_t=D_T ũ, u_tt=D_T(D_T ũ), ∂_{x_j}u=D_{S_j}ũ, ∂_{x_jx_j}u=D_{S_j}(D_{S_j}ũ), and ∂_{x_j}u_t=D_{S_j}(D_T ũ). For any scalar or vector field h on Ω use the same total extension convention (arbitrary off Ω) and write ∂_t h=D_T h and ∂_{x_j}h=D_{S_j}h on Ω. These are derivatives of the original germs wherever differentiable. Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise, and |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|² is the Frobenius square.

binders.type: scalar or vector field on Ω

definitions.definition: For (x,t)∈Ω, e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². The normalization contains no factor 1/2. When a total time function is needed extend e by zero at t≤0.

definitions.type: family of real flux functions on Ω
definitions.definition: flux is the family denoted g_j: for j=1,…,n and (x,t)∈Ω, g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩. Extend by zero at nonpositive times when total functions are needed.

For a scalar or vector function f on a topological space A with a distinguished zero in its codomain, tsupport f is the closure in A of {z : f(z)≠0}. Compact topological support means that this closed set is compact.

argument.text: By H001, ũ is smooth on the open set Ω. Apply M008 with this domain and map to obtain smoothness of its Fréchet derivative field. Evaluation at each fixed direction T or S_j is continuous linear, so composition preserves smoothness and gives smoothness of u_t and ∂_{x_j}u. Apply M008 again to these smooth fields on the same open domain and evaluate at the fixed directions to get smoothness of u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u_t and ∂_{x_jx_j}u. These assertions use only positive-time germs of D005. In the finite-dimensional real Euclidean codomain, inner products and norm squares are finite sums of products of smooth coordinate functions. Finite sums and products preserve smoothness; thus e, each g_j, and all three inner-product terms in the claimed output are smooth. Applying M008 to e and g_j and evaluating at T and S_j also proves smoothness of ∂_t e and ∂_{x_j}g_j. Fixed-time spatial sections of each function are smooth by composition with the affine inclusion of Xn.

produces.statement: All of e, ∂_t e, g_j, ∂_{x_j}g_j, ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩ are jointly smooth on Ω and have smooth fixed-positive-time spatial sections, for every j=1,…,n.

argument.text: Fix tau>0. Since 0<tau/2<3tau/2, H005 at these two endpoints supplies a compact spatial set with u=q outside it at every time in the closed interval.

produces.statement: There exists a compact C⊂Xn such that u(x,r)=q for all x∉C and r∈[tau/2,3tau/2].

argument.text: Choose Cwin from F002 and define Owin. A compact subset of the Euclidean space Xn is closed, so Owin is open and contained in Ω. On Owin, ũ is identically q. Apply M009 at each point of Owin to ũ and the constant map q, whose derivative is zero. Thus its whole derivative field is zero on Owin. Apply M009 again, now to that derivative field and the zero continuous-linear-map-valued function, to obtain zero second derivative there. Evaluation in T and S_j shows that u_t, ∂_{x_j}u, u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u_t and ∂_{x_jx_j}u all vanish on Owin. Consequently e, g_j and the three listed inner-product terms vanish there by their definitions. Since e and g_j are identically zero on this open set, further applications of M009 to e and g_j and the constant scalar zero give ∂_t e=0 and ∂_{x_j}g_j=0 throughout Owin. No conclusion about derivatives at the time endpoints is needed.

produces.statement: Cwin is compact and closed. All of e, ∂_t e, g_j, ∂_{x_j}g_j, ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩ vanish at (x,r) for every x∉Cwin and r∈(tau/2,3tau/2), for every coordinate index j=1,…,n.

argument.text: For every interior time r, F003 puts the nonzero set of each spatial section inside Cwin. Closure of that nonzero set is still contained in Cwin since Cwin is closed; this closure is tsupport by D014. It is compact as a closed subset of the compact Cwin. Combine this with the joint smoothness in F001. Cwin witnesses all support assertions simultaneously for this tau. The conclusion no longer depends on its private identity; existential elimination and universal introduction for arbitrary tau prove the full claimed output, including all three inner-product terms.
